name: Data integrity, sync, and the screens agreeing with each other
summary: On one device the desk keeps its counts straight: after a split, a removal, a restore and figures typed, the work bar, the chips, the summary, the Estate Inventory Report, the Court Inventory, the Disposition Ledger and the CSV all agreed (9 items, $8,230). The weak point is two devices working one job. The desk reads the sheet only when the tab is opened or a client is picked. The manifest merges whole lines on updatedAt, and agent writes stamp that clock the same way a person's edit does. So a device holding an old copy overwrites the other device's work on any line it touches. Driven through the real controls against the real server merge, that lost a typed name, a $1,250 dealer-quote figure, a person's condition grade and a review tick. It replaced a typed name with Agent One's guess and brought back eight lines another device had removed, named and valued. Three accuracy defects reach the papers a trust officer or executor reads. A written approval stays complete after the line is sent somewhere else, so the ledger shows both fiduciaries authorising a donation they never approved. A deliberate clear of a wrong approval or recipient comes back from a device that never saw the clear. And the client's Drive workbook in the counsel-shared folder is rebuilt from whichever device saved last, from its own possibly stale copy. Work can also be stranded on a device with no sign: an edit made within 2.5 s of closing or reloading, or an edit whose write failed before a reload, never reaches the sheet, and the chip disappears. When the sheet is slow or unreachable, the desk redraws on a timer and after every edit. That redraw saves a half-typed name and sends it to Agent Two. A cold desk says "No items yet" and "0 of 0 reviewed" while the bars correctly say loading. It even records a permanent "Filed with court: 0 items, $0" snapshot. The fix that matters most is per-field clocks on the fields a person owns, plus a sheet read before every run, paper and snapshot, so two concierges can work a 600-line house at once. The approval must also be tied to the destination and recipient it approved.
works_well: Single-device counts agree across every surface after split, remove and restore: work bar 4 of 9 reviewed, Summary 9 items $8,230, Estate Inventory Report 9 items $8,230, CSV 9 rows, Court Inventory DRAFT naming the 4 unvalued lines (SYN/e7.js, out/e7.txt).

The bars honour 'an empty store is unread': loading… on a cold device, 'sheet unreachable: this device's copy' after a failed read, and the 15 s retry brings the lines in once the signal returns (SYN/e1.js, e13.js).

A reload in the middle of a naming run leaves no stuck state: the 19 lines named before the reload were on the sheet, and the work bar offered Name 30 shots, Check 6 rooms and Value 19 lines (SYN/e4.js, out/e4.txt).
Sends and close-out filings (Send request, the estate package, the ledger and records filers) read the sheet first and refuse with a named reason when they cannot (havellin.html:32826, 18064, 34626).
Item-number collisions converge the same way on every device: the earlier-born line keeps the number and the other takes the next free one (out/e12.txt).
Custody logs union and release signers union across devices; serial, channel, dealer route and field note survive a newer copy that lacks them (sticky list, held equal on app and server).

On one device Agent One leaves alone a row a person named while the run was out (agentApplyResult's blank-row guard, havellin.html:37701), and Agent Two's run tail waits for the person to leave the box rather than redrawing under them.
The split repaint matched the full render in every check (no drift after + Another item in this photo), and the bars' lines (desk-stat-*) matched a full render after every edit driven.
measurements: Desk sheet reads while the tab stays open: loadMedia 1 -> 1 over 40 s (SYN/e2.js, out/e2.txt). There is no timer; it reads on tab open or client pick only.

Two-device same-line edit: device A's name, $1,250 value, condition Excellent and review on #10 were all gone from the sheet one qty edit later from device B; device A's typed name on #26 became 'White porcelain dinner plates' qty 8, $320 after B pressed Name 1 shot (out/e2.txt).

Resurrection: 8 lines removed on device A came back live, named and valued, after device B (stale) pressed Name 24 shots; live lines on the sheet went 16 -> 26 and $3,540 of figures returned (SYN/e6.js, out/e6.txt).
Stranded edit: a name typed, Tab, page reloaded 1 s later: 0 beforeunload dialogs, 0 saveMedia in the next 20 s, the sheet still blank (SYN/e3b.js).
Offline then reload: 2 saveMedia attempts aborted, beforeunload fired, then 0 saveMedia in the 60 s after the reload, the chip gone, and the device showing the edit the sheet lacks (SYN/e3.js).

Half-typed name committed by a sheet-read redraw: 'Mahogany secretary desk with gla' saved and sent to agentValue, valued $60 (SYN/e13.js); 'Nightstand, mahogany with' saved, the rest of the typing lost (SYN/e17.js).
Workbook vs manifest after two devices edited different lines: manifest #4 $120, the workbook rows sent by the last device #4 $80 (SYN/e14.js).
Cold desk while loading: work bar '0 of 0 reviewed', body 'No items yet…', Job Admin '5 derived items' (8 once read); a manual line got #1, renumbered to #32 after the merge (SYN/e1.js).
Cold estate desk with the sheet unreachable: Snapshot offered; recorded 'Filed with court: 0 items, $0' and synced it while the sheet held 9 lines (SYN/e10b.js).
Vehicle import on a cold device: 2 live lines for one car (#40 $38,500 and #41 unvalued), the Court Inventory lists it twice, 0 Possible duplicates groups (SYN/e8.js).
A press straight from a box is lost: 3 of 3 first presses (the No value yet chip, the Not yet decided chip, Estate Inventory PDF) did nothing; the second press worked (SYN/e9.js, e9b.js).

Repaint-by-id vs full render: 4 of 4 figure edits left the group head's value total stale; category set in the record left the row's icon and badges stale, and on Firearms the NFA tick and 'Not cleared to carry' panel were missing until a full render (SYN/e5.js, e5b.js, e5c.js).

Agent Two landing under a cursor: after 20 s in one box, 23 of 24 valued rows showed a blank Total, the state line read 'Valuing… 24 of 24', and the work bar still offered 'Value 24 lines' (SYN/e18.js).
verifier_note:
The SYN report holds up well. I reproduced every defect it claims myself, through the real controls. I wrote my own rig for this: one Chromium running two real app contexts (device A and device B) against one shared sheet, with saveMedia merged through the real server _mergeMediaItems lifted from saveInventory.gs. The rig is SYN-verify/two.js. The auditor injected device A's edits by hand; my rig drives both devices. I also ran a pure merge test of the app's mergeMediaItems and the server's merge side by side. All of it is under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-app/107e11dc-7b83-525c-829c-97f2e5cca8f9/scratchpad/audit/SYN-verify/ (scripts v1 to v13b, outputs in out/).

Corrections to the report:
- SYN-09: its claim that nothing on the desk points at the doubled car is wrong. The desk draws a 'Duplicate imports' warning (_renderDuplicateImportNotice, havellin.html:37028, drawn at 40271). The auditor only checked agentDuplicateGroups. The base defect is already in Open work, so this is a duplicate of a known item.
- SYN-12: the reach is real but narrower than 'about once per row'. A name typed and then the PDF pressed works. A figure typed and then a work-bar button or chip pressed, or a name typed and then a chip pressed, loses the press.
- SYN-17's per-line size is from MANUAL.md and BUILD_HISTORY.md, not CLAUDE.md, and its consequences are reasoning, not measurement.
- SYN-07's Shared Drive duplicate-workbook risk is reasoning from code: it rests on the codebase's own warning about getFilesByName.

Severity changes: I moved SYN-02 from fix-now to high, because the tombstone-loses-to-a-later-edit property is already documented in CLAUDE.md's Data section. I moved SYN-09 down to medium as a known item.

SYN-01 and SYN-03 stay fix-now:
- SYN-01 loses data and puts wrong figures and names on the papers.
- SYN-03 needs only one device and puts the fiduciaries' names, on the Disposition Ledger, against a release they never approved.

Something the report does not stress: Agent Two's automatic run (agentValueAuto) is a write the app makes by itself, yet it stamps updatedAt like a person's edit (_avWrite calls _invTouch). That sits against CLAUDE.md's rule that a write the app makes on its own never moves the clock, and it widens SYN-01.

findings.title: A device with an old copy overwrites the other device's work on any line it touches: names, values, grades and reviews are lost, and a typed name is replaced by Agent One's guess
findings.where: Whole desk, two devices. Causes: _invRefreshFromCloud reads only on tab open or client pick (havellin.html:36884, called from 25499 and 36879); mergeMediaItems resolves a whole line on updatedAt, sticky fields aside (havellin.html:29131; server _mergeMediaItems, saveInventory.gs:593); every agent writer stamps the clock through _invTouch (_agWrite 37631, _avWrite 38629, _arWrite 38357); agentNameShots sends from the local copy without reading the sheet (37736); agentApplyResult's blank-row guard reads the local copy (37701).
findings.evidence: SYN/e2.js with the real server merge lifted from saveInventory.gs (SYN/srv.js), output in out/e2.txt. Device A's saves on the sheet: #10 'Henredon walnut dresser, nine drawers', $1,250 Dealer quote, condition Excellent, reviewed; #26 typed 'Mahogany secretary desk with glazed top', reviewed. Device B (this page) kept the desk open: 'loadMedia calls 1 -> 1' after 40 s, and its row still read 'Walnut dresser'. B changed #10's Qty to 2. The sheet then held {name 'Walnut dresser', namedBy agent, fmv 900, reviewed 0}: A's name, figure, source, grade and review were gone. B pressed 'Name 1 shot'; the sheet's #26 became 'White porcelain dinner plates', qty 8, $320 by Agent Two, the review dropped. Device A reopening merges to the same loss. Server-merge pairs (SYN/m1.js) show the same for a person's grade and review against a stale Agent Two run, and for 'Not duplicates' (dupOK) against a stale room check. The code says it outright (havellin.html:28966): 'two people editing DIFFERENT items ... still clobber each other' applies within an item. KNOWN: Open work's 'two devices ... each start their own automatic Agent Two run ... the later save winning' is the narrow case; the impact here is a person's work lost to an old copy's edit or an agent write.
findings.tc_impact: Anthony and Ashley splitting a 600-line house that evening, or the iPad open from a pickup day, silently undo each other's names, values and ticks. Nothing on screen says the copy is old. A corrected name reverts to the agent's guess, and a reviewed line goes back to unreviewed or carries a figure nobody looked at. The attorney receives a schedule where a dealer-quoted $1,250 dresser reads $900 'General estimate', or a secretary desk listed as eight dinner plates.
findings.proposal: (1) Per-field clocks for the fields a person owns on a line: objectName with namedBy, category with catBy, qty, fmv, unitVal, valSource, valNote and valDate, condition with condBy, disposition, reviewed with valReviewed, dupOK and deletedAt. Write them as ref.at[field] beside updatedAt, merged field by field in mergeMediaItems and _mergeMediaItems, with a test holding the two equal (the jobs already do this with job.at['kind:key']). (2) Agent writes carry the time the request was sent, so a field a person changed after that is never overwritten. In _agWrite, _avWrite and _arWrite, skip any field whose at[] is newer than the request's sentAt. (3) Read the sheet before Name N shots, Check N rooms, Value N lines and the bulk bar's Mark reviewed and Remove lines, as sendApprovalRequest already does. Also read it every 60 s while the desk is open, through _invRenderWhenIdle. When a read changes anything, the TC sees a toast such as 'Ashley's iPad changed 12 lines: shown'.
findings.vnote:
Both devices were real app pages in my rig.
1. B opened the desk, then A opened it.
2. A typed a name and a $1,250 Total on e10 and ticked review, using the row's own boxes. The sheet held all three.
3. B made no loadMedia call in the next 15 s (1 before, 1 after) and still showed 'Walnut dresser'.
4. B changed e10's Qty to 2. The sheet's e10 became the agent's name, fmv 900 (B's old 450 x 2) and reviewed 0. A's name, figure and review were gone.
5. A typed a name on e26 and it reached the sheet. B then pressed 'Name 1 shot' (its copy still blank). The sheet's e26 became 'White porcelain dinner plates', namedBy agent, qty 8, $320. A reopened its desk and saw the same loss.

Code: there is no timer read on the desk. _invRefreshFromCloud runs only from tab open (25499) and client pick (36879). Both merges keep the whole line with the newer updatedAt, sticky fields aside (havellin.html:29131, saveInventory.gs:593). _agWrite, _avWrite and _arWrite all call _invTouch.

The narrow Open-work item (two automatic Agent Two runs) does not cover a person's work being overwritten. The per-field clocks the proposal asks for are not on the Decided list. The code comment at 29004 shows the developer avoided them; Anthony did not rule them out.

Key lines: '3 sheet e10 after B qty: {"name":"Walnut dresser","namedBy":"agent","fmv":900,"reviewed":0,"qty":"2"}' and '6 sheet e26 after B Name shots: {"name":"White porcelain dinner plates","namedBy":"agent","qty":8,"fmv":320,"valuedBy":"agent"}'

findings.title: Lines removed on one device come back named and valued when a device with an old copy runs Name shots
findings.where: Work bar Name N shots on the second device. Causes: agentShotGroups and agentNameableRefs read the local copy (havellin.html:37546, 37555); _agWrite stamps updatedAt (28945), so the old live copy's newer clock beats the tombstone (mergeMediaItems 29131; saveInventory.gs:593).
findings.evidence: SYN/e6.js, out/e6.txt. A cleanout trust job with 24 unnamed Items shots. Device A's removal of 8 drawer shots (deletedAt) was on the sheet, leaving 16 live lines. Device B (stale) was offered 'Name 24 shots' and pressed it. The sheet afterwards: all 8 LIVE again, e.g. 's0:LIVE "Tufted linen three-seat sofa" $350 ... s6:LIVE "Sterling silver candlesticks, Gorham" $1200'. Live lines on the sheet went 16 -> 26, and agentIdentify was sent all 24 shots (20+4). CLAUDE.md records 'A tombstone still loses to a later edit of the same item from a device that never saw the removal'. The new impact is that an agent run, which nobody experiences as an edit, is that later edit, and it brings back a whole bulk removal.
findings.tc_impact: The Ellison pattern (hundreds of drawer lines cleared with Remove lines) undoes itself the moment the other device names shots. The TC pays for the agent calls twice, re-removes the lines, and may not notice that removed junk is back on the Court Inventory and in the totals.
findings.proposal: deletedAt gets its own clock under SYN-01's per-field merge: a removal beats any later edit to a field other than a Restore. Until that lands, agentNameShots reads the sheet first and refuses to send a line the sheet holds removed, and _agWrite never writes a line whose sheet copy is removed. The TC presses Name shots and sees 'Named 16 of 16. 8 removed on the other device were left alone'.
findings.vnote:
Both devices were real app pages on job 9700, a trust estate with 24 unnamed Items shots.
1. A ticked 8 rows and pressed the bulk bar's Remove lines, confirming 'Remove 8 lines'. The sheet showed 16 live lines and 8 removed.
2. B, whose desk was opened earlier, was offered 'Name 24 shots' and pressed it. It sent agentIdentify all 24 shots (20+4).
3. Afterwards all 8 were live on the sheet again, named and valued ('s0:LIVE "Tufted linen three-seat sofa" $350 … s6:LIVE "Sterling silver candlesticks, Gorham" $1200'). Live lines on the sheet went 16 -> 26. A, reopening its desk, saw 26 live lines.

Why high, not fix-now: CLAUDE.md's Data section already records that 'A tombstone still loses to a later edit of the same item from a device that never saw the removal'. The new impact is that an agent run, which nobody experiences as an edit, is that later edit, and it undoes a whole bulk removal.

findings.title: A written approval stays complete after the line is sent somewhere else; the ledger then shows both fiduciaries authorising a donation they never approved
findings.where: The row's Where it goes and Who takes it boxes, and the bulk bar's Set disposition and Set recipient. Causes: invApprovalComplete reads only authBy and approvalDate (havellin.html:31383); _invEdit clears nothing on a disposition or channel edit (29700); the merge keeps authBy, approvalDate and channel sticky but not disposition (INV_STICKY_FIELDS 28996). Readers that trust it: signoutGroups (31648), _invAwaitingApproval (31221), dispositionLedger (34374).
findings.evidence: SYN/e11.js, out/e11.txt. Ashworth #1 Harbor scene oil painting was signed by Thomas and Nora Ashworth on the 2026-10-12 request for 'Auction · Kodner Galleries'. Changing Where it goes to Donate and then Who takes it to Goodwill: invApprovalComplete stayed true, the Releases bar still read '3 items need written approval' (unchanged), and the sign-out rows offered 'donation|goodwill palm beach: ready #1'. The Disposition Ledger printed '1 Harbor scene oil painting Donate Goodwill Palm Beach Thomas Ashworth; Nora Ashworth (Oct 12, 2026)'. The merge makes the same hybrid without anyone's choice: {Distribute -> Margaret, approved}@10 merged with an old {Sell, value typed}@20 gives 'disposition Sell, channel Margaret Ashworth, authBy Thomas Ashworth; Nora Ashworth'.
findings.tc_impact: One mis-tap on a $2,400 painting's dropdown, or the other device's old copy, turns a signed auction approval into an apparently signed donation. The iPad then offers the painting to Goodwill on pickup day. The trust officer signs a ledger that puts their names to a release they never gave. That is the release-integrity breach the whole approval process exists to prevent.
findings.proposal: Bind an approval to what it approved. Record approval (invSaveApproval), and Record the signed request, write authFor: {disposition, channel trimmed and case-folded} beside authBy. invApprovalComplete answers false when the line's disposition or recipient no longer match authFor, and the line goes back on the next request headed 'changed after it was signed: for re-approval'. The row's chip reads 'approval was for Auction · Kodner'. A recipient's spelling corrected without changing the person is allowed through samePerson. The ledger prints the approval against the destination it was given for. authFor joins the manifest's save list and the sticky list on both sides, with the test holding the two equal.
findings.vnote:
One device, Ashworth #1. e01 was signed for 'Auction · Kodner Galleries' by Thomas and Nora Ashworth.
1. I changed the row's Where it goes select to Donate. No dialog appeared. invApprovalComplete stayed true, and e01 stayed off _invAwaitingApproval (still e04, e07, e10).
2. I typed Goodwill Palm Beach in Who takes it. Again no dialog and no change.
3. The row's sub-line showed nothing. The Releases bar was unchanged ('3 items need written approval…').
4. signoutGroups offered 'donation|goodwill palm beach ready:#1'.
5. The Disposition Ledger printed 'Harbor scene oil painting Donate Goodwill Palm Beach Thomas Ashworth; Nora Ashworth (Oct 12, 2026)'.
6. The next approval request would carry e04, e07 and e10, not e01.

Code: invApprovalComplete reads only authBy and approvalDate (havellin.html:31383). _invEdit clears neither on a disposition or channel edit. approvalRequestChanged applies only to a draft still waiting (32647). This needs no second device: one mis-tap puts the fiduciaries' names against a release they never gave.

findings.title: A deliberate clear of a sticky field (a wrong approval, a wrong recipient) is undone by any newer edit from a device that never saw the clear
findings.where: The item record's Authorized By and Channel / Recipient boxes. Causes: invStickyValue honours clearedAt only when the clearing copy is the winner (havellin.html:29017; server _invStickyValue, saveInventory.gs:460); invMergeApprovals returns 'the sticky rule's answer' when its base is empty (29080 on; saveInventory.gs:525).
findings.evidence: SYN/m1.js on the real server merge, output out/m1.txt. A clears a wrongly recorded approval at t=10 (authBy '', authBySetAt 10, clearedAt.authBy 10). B, which never saw the clear, sets the condition at t=20. Result: authBy 'Thomas Ashworth; Nora Ashworth', approvalDate '2026-10-12'; the approval is back. A clears the recipient 'Ashley Jerome' at t=10; B edits the value at t=20. Result: channel 'Ashley Jerome'; a Havellin person is back as the recipient.
findings.tc_impact: The TC corrects a mis-recorded release, or takes a staff member off a line, and it quietly comes back after the other device's next unrelated edit. The line then leaves the house 'approved', or sits under a refusal rule the TC thought was settled. Nothing on screen says so.
findings.proposal: Treat clearedAt[key] as a clock in its own right on both sides: the merged field is the value, or the clear, whichever is newer. For authBy, compare against authBySetAt and authAdds as invMergeApprovals already does for names. This falls out of SYN-01's per-field clocks if those land. Otherwise fix invStickyValue alone (app and server, held equal by tests/media-merge.test.js): take the loser's clear when lose.clearedAt[key] is newer than the winner's value was set.
findings.vnote:
I ran the real app mergeMediaItems (lifted with tests/harness.js) and the real server _mergeMediaItems on the same pairs.
- A clears authBy at t=10 (authBySetAt and clearedAt.authBy, as _invEdit stamps them). B, which never saw the clear, edits the condition at t=20. Both merges return authBy 'Thomas Ashworth; Nora Ashworth' and approvalDate 2026-10-12, in either argument order.
- A clears channel 'Ashley Jerome' at t=10. B edits the value at t=20. Both return channel 'Ashley Jerome'.
- Control: when the clearing copy is the newer one, the clear holds.

This goes against the code's own stated intent (comments at 29004 and 29063: 'A CORRECTION IS NOT UNDONE BY A STALE COPY … a deliberate clear stamps clearedAt.authBy'). The cause is invMergeApprovals: when its base is empty it returns 'the sticky rule's answer'. invStickyValue honours clearedAt only on the winning copy.

findings.title: When the sheet is slow or unreachable, the desk redraws on a timer and after every edit, saving a half-typed name and sending it to Agent Two
findings.where: _invRefreshFromCloud's 'if (changed || made) renderInventoryTab()' (havellin.html:36900), reached from the 15 s retry _invCloudRetryArm (36911). Also _scheduleInventorySync's held-workbook branch 'refreshPhotoRefs(jobId, function(){ renderInventoryTab(); })', which redraws whatever the answer, 2.5 s after every edit on a desk that has not read the sheet (40463). The comment at 36897 says 'never on a timer that could redraw over somebody typing'.
findings.evidence: SYN/e13.js, out/e13.txt: the sheet unreachable at open, the TC typing in #26's name box, the signal back. After the retry, value 'Mahogany secretary desk with gla', focused false; the line saved with that name, agentValue sent [['Mahogany secretary desk with gla']], valued $60. SYN/e17.js, out/e17.txt: the sheet still unreachable, one name edited, then typing ', mahogany with brass pu' in the next row. After the held-workbook read the box read 'Nightstand, mahogany with', unfocused, and that was the saved name; the rest of the typing went nowhere. loadMedia was called 3 times.
findings.tc_impact: This bites in a house with poor signal, the iPad's pickup day the guide describes, and on any cold device. Every couple of edits the screen jumps out from under the TC, cuts a name mid-word and saves it. Agent Two then researches the fragment, which costs a call and gives a wrong value until the TC notices and retypes.
findings.proposal: Route both callbacks through _invRenderWhenIdle (it already waits for focusout and asks again). In _scheduleInventorySync, render only when the read changed something, as _invRefreshFromCloud does. Hold the 'Workbook held' read to once per job per 15 s rather than once per edit.
findings.vnote:
I drove both paths with continuous typing in a name box. The fixture: a cold session whose sheet holds one line this device lacks, the first read failing.
- (a) The 15 s retry: 'Mahogany secretary desk with glazed bookcase top and brass pulls' typed over 25 s. After the retry the box read 'Mahogany secretary desk with glazed bo' and was unfocused. That fragment was saved and sent to agentValue, and came back valued $60.
- (b) The held-workbook read, with the sheet still unreachable: one name edited, then typing in the next row's name. The box was cut to 'Mahogany secretary d', saved, and sent to agentValue.

Code: _invRefreshFromCloud calls renderInventoryTab directly on a change (36900), and it is reached from the 15 s timer _invCloudRetryArm (36911). Its comment says it is never run on a timer. _scheduleInventorySync's held branch redraws whatever the answer (40463).

findings.title: Work can be stranded on a device: an edit within 2.5 s of closing or reloading is never sent and never challenged, and after a reload a failed write is never resent
findings.where: beforeunload asks only _pendingCount(), the failed-write queue (havellin.html:42393, 41981), not the 2.5 s debounce (_invSyncTimer, 40430), the outbox (_outbox) or a request in flight. refreshPhotoRefs merges the sheet into the device's copy but never schedules a save when the device's copy is newer (27298). The chip counts writes, not edits (42054).
findings.evidence: SYN/e3b.js: name typed, Tab, page reloaded 1 s later. 'dialogs on reload: []', 'saveMedia sent: 0' over the next 20 s, the device showing the name and the sheet ''. SYN/e3.js, out/e3.txt: offline with saveMedia aborted, two edits, chip '⚠ 1 unsaved change — retrying…', beforeunload fired, reload. 'calls in the 60 s after reload: getThumbnails,loadMedia' (no saveMedia), the chip gone, the device showing 'Mahogany secretary desk, glazed top', the sheet holding "". It reaches the sheet only with the next edit on that job from that device. The same gap applies to an agent run's answers landing inside the last 2.5 s.
findings.tc_impact: The last value of the evening, or an hour's work done through a dead connection, sits on one laptop with nothing on screen saying so. Ashley's iPad shows the old lines. Her next edit of them wins, and the laptop's work is lost for good on its next read (SYN-01).
findings.proposal: Count _invSyncTimer, _outbox and in-flight sends in _pendingCount, so the existing guard covers them; flush a waiting manifest write on visibilitychange 'hidden' and on pagehide. On every sheet read (refreshPhotoRefs), compare each local line with the sheet's copy. Where the device's copy is newer or missing from the sheet, schedule _scheduleInventorySync and show the chip as 'N lines on this device not yet on the sheet'. This persists no queue: it derives the need from the data already kept in localStorage.
findings.decided_conflict: Decided: do not re-propose 'Persisting the retry queue to localStorage'. This proposal persists nothing new: the edits are already in hav_media_<id>, and the resend is derived from comparing them with the sheet on the next read.
findings.vnote:
The Apps Script URL was set in Settings (localStorage), so the reloaded page booted with it, as a real device would.
- (1) A name typed, Tab, reload 1 s later: no beforeunload dialog. No saveMedia in the 20 s after the reload, the desk reopened. The device held the name and the sheet held ''. The chip was gone.
- (2) saveMedia aborting, four edits: the chip said '⚠ 1 unsaved change — retrying…'. beforeunload fired once and the reload went ahead. After the reload, only loadMedia in 45 s, with no saveMedia. The device held both names and $140, the sheet held '' and 'Nightstand'. The chip was gone.

Code: _pendingCount counts only _pendingWrites (41981). The 2.5 s debounce, the 250 ms outbox and an in-flight request are not counted. saveMedia is posted only from _scheduleInventorySync (40445), so nothing resends after a reload until the next edit on that job.

The proposal derives the resend from data already in localStorage and persists no queue, so it does not conflict with the Decided item 'Persisting the retry queue to localStorage'.

findings.title: The client's Drive workbook in the counsel-shared Estate Inventory folder is rebuilt from whichever device saved last, from its own copy, and is found by a lookup the project says comes back empty on a Shared Drive
findings.where: App: _scheduleInventorySync posts saveInventory built from the device's own copy (buildInventoryPayload, havellin.html:40322; gated only on _invCloudSeen, 40458, which is true for the whole session after the first read). Server: saveInventory rebuilds the 'Inventory' sheet from payload.rows (saveInventory.gs:64-98, _writeInventorySheet 105), not from the merged manifest saveMediaStore has just written. It finds the workbook with target.getFilesByName(name) (saveInventory.gs:85), the call _filesNamedInFolder's comment (main-sync.gs:1690-1703) says 'can come back empty ... every save creates another file' on a Shared Drive.
findings.evidence: SYN/e14.js, out/e14.txt: device A corrected #4 to $120 and its save landed; device B (this page) typed #23's value. Manifest on the sheet: '#4 lamps: 120 | #23: 275'. The workbook rows B sent: '#4 lamps FMV: 80'. The getFilesByName duplicate risk comes from reading the code, not from observation: this environment has no Drive.
findings.tc_impact: The attorney who opens the shared folder reads whichever device saved last. Values flip between devices' views, and the workbook disagrees with the PDF schedules filed beside it. If the lookup comes back empty on the Shared Drive, every desk edit (debounced 2.5 s) adds another 'Estate Inventory — HVL-…' spreadsheet to counsel's folder.
findings.proposal: Server: build the workbook rows from the merged store entry saveMediaStore just wrote, for example a saveInventory that names the job and reads store[jobId].items after the merge, with the app sending only the derived flags (docSet, onProbate, netLabel). Find the file with _filesNamedInFolder, updating the oldest copy in place and trashing extras, as _fileBlobByName does. Bump BACKEND_VERSION and tell Anthony the redeploy fixes counsel's workbook.
findings.vnote:
Both devices were real app pages.
1. A typed #4 to $120. Both its saveMedia and its saveInventory carried 'Estimated FMV=120'.
2. B, still stale, typed #23 to $275. The merged manifest on the sheet then read #4 $120 and #23 $275.
3. B's saveInventory came last, and its rows carried '#4 Estimated FMV=80'.

The server rebuilds the workbook from payload.rows (saveInventory.gs:64-98, _writeInventorySheet at 105), not from the merged store. The workbook sits in Estate Inventory, the folder shared with counsel.

The second half of the finding is plausible, not observed (no Drive here): saveInventory.gs:85 finds the file with target.getFilesByName, which main-sync.gs:1690-1703 warns can come back empty on a Shared Drive and then make another file on every save.

findings.title: A cold or unreachable desk claims none: '0 of 0 reviewed', 'No items yet. Open a room…', papers refusing 'nothing in the inventory', and a permanent zero-item Snapshot
findings.where: Only the bars and the appraisers' form ask _invManifestUnread (havellin.html:48149; readers 36280 and 48182). The work bar, the rows' empty state (renderInventoryTab, 40217), Job Admin's count, printEstateInventoryReport (31022), exportInventoryCSV (31189), addInventoryManualItem and takeInventorySnapshot (30265) read the empty cache as fact.
findings.evidence: SYN/e1.js, out/e1.txt, a cold device with the read in flight. Bars 'loading…', but the work bar read '0 of 0 reviewed', the body 'No items yet. Open a room on the Job Plan and shoot it…', and Job Admin '0 of 5 ticked · 5 derived items still open' (8 once read). '+ Add line item' gave the new line #1 (renumbered #32 after the merge). With the read failed, the body still said 'No items yet' and the history bar '0 removed'. SYN/e10b.js, out/e10b.txt: a cold estate desk with the sheet unreachable offered More ▾ Snapshot; it recorded 'Filed with court: 0 items, $0' on the job and synced it while the sheet held 9 lines. A snapshot is never deleted, only voided.
findings.tc_impact: A concierge opening the desk on the iPad in a dead spot is told the house has no items. They may start shooting again, add lines by hand, or take a 'Filed with court' snapshot that permanently records an empty estate in the job's trail. The papers' 'nothing to report' and 'nothing to export' alerts say the same untruth.
findings.proposal: One rule, _invManifestUnread, read wherever the desk draws or acts off the list. Until it clears, the work bar reads 'reading the sheet…' (or 'sheet unreachable: this device's copy'); the empty state says 'This device has not read this client's items yet'. Snapshot, the papers, CSV and + Add line item refuse by name ('Not taken: this device has not read the inventory from the sheet. Check the connection and try again'). takeInventorySnapshot also reads the sheet first, as the sends do.
findings.vnote:
The fixture is a device that has never held 9601's manifest.
- With the read held, the bars read 'loading…', while the work bar read '0 of 0 reviewed', the body 'No items yet.' and Job Admin '0 of 5 ticked · 5 derived items still open'.
- Calling printEstateInventoryReport at once gave 'There is nothing in the inventory to report yet.', with no read first.
- After the read failed, the bars read 'sheet unreachable: this device’s copy' and the body still said 'No items yet.'.
- More ▾ offered Snapshot. Pressing it recorded 'Filed with court 0 items $0' on the job and synced it (3 job writes) while the sheet held 9 live lines.

Code: takeInventorySnapshot has no read-first and no refusal of an unread or empty list (30265). Only five places ask _invManifestUnread.

findings.title: KNOWN: the vehicle import on a cold device creates a second line for the same car, which the Court Inventory lists twice with no duplicate flag
findings.where: From the Estimate Walkthrough card (_renderInventoryImportPanel, havellin.html:36211). materializeVehicle mints stableId jobId+'_veh'+vehId+'_'+Date.now() (36202), so two devices' imports never merge into one line; its only guard (_importedSourceSet) reads the local copy.
findings.evidence: KNOWN: Open work records that 'The vehicle import has no _invCloudSeen guard ... re-offers a vehicle on a cold device'. New impact, measured in SYN/e8.js, out/e8.txt. The laptop's line #40 '2019 Mercedes-Benz E 450 sedan' at $38,500 was on the sheet. The cold iPad with the read failed offered 'Add →' and created #41. After the merge, two live lines; the Court Inventory names the car under the Vehicles subtotal twice ('…Good dealer quote' and '…Good not stated'); agentDuplicateGroups returned 0 groups.
findings.tc_impact: Often the estate's most valuable tangible asset is double-counted. The schedule stays DRAFT until the second line is valued, and once the TC values it the car is counted twice in the total sent to counsel. Nothing on the desk points at it.
findings.proposal: Make the line's id the vehicle's own (jobId+'_veh'+vehId), as collectionLineId does for collections, so two devices make the same line and the merge unifies them. Withhold the import card until _invCloudSeen, as collectionLinesEnsure waits. Add sourceVehId to Possible duplicates (two live lines with one sourceVehId are always a pair).
findings.vnote:
Already in Open work: 'The vehicle import has no _invCloudSeen guard and reads live lines only, so it re-offers a vehicle on a cold device'.

I reproduced the consequence. The cold desk offered 'Add →'. After the read landed there were two live lines, #40 (stableId …_1792984982034, $38,500) and #41 (…_1793071384832, no value). The Court Inventory listed the car on 2 rows.

The auditor's 'no duplicate flag' / 'nothing on the desk points at it' is wrong. The desk drew '⚠ Duplicate imports. These lines came from the same estimate entry more than once…' (_renderDuplicateImportNotice, havellin.html:37028, drawn at 40271; _invDuplicateImports returned 1 group). agentDuplicateGroups returning 0 is the wrong reader to check.

New detail worth keeping: materializeVehicle mints the id with Date.now() (36202), so the merge can never unify two imports. The proposal (an id built from the vehicle, waiting for _invCloudSeen) is sound and allowed.

findings.where: Work bar and More ▾: printEstateInventoryReport (havellin.html:31014), printCourtInventory (34030), printTrustSchedule (34219), printContentsRecord (35561), printAppraisalWorklist (35356), exportInventoryCSV (31186) and takeInventorySnapshot (30265). findings.vnote:
Code: printEstateInventoryReport, printCourtInventory, printTrustSchedule, printContentsRecord, printAppraisalWorklist, printDispositionLedger, printApprovalRequest, exportInventoryCSV and takeInventorySnapshot never call refreshPhotoRefs. I checked the first 80 lines of each. The work-bar buttons call them directly (39408, 39412, 39432).

The sends do read first: sendProbatePackage at 18064, sendApprovalRequest at 32826, and the close-out filer at 34626, each refusing when unread.

findings.title: Two devices issue the same next item number; the later-born line's number moves after a paper has already cited it
findings.where: _invAssignItemNos issues numbers off the local high-water mark and resolves collisions in favour of the earliest ts (havellin.html:29230-29272); a split line takes its source photograph's ts (invSplitItemN, 28749).
findings.evidence: SYN/e12.js, out/e12.txt: device B split the dresser's photograph and named the line 'Gilt overmantel mirror'. It took #32, and B's printed approval request read '32 Gilt overmantel mirror'. Device A's split of the painting's photograph, saved earlier, also carried #32. After B read the sheet: '#32 Carved giltwood frame (spare)', '#33 Gilt overmantel mirror'.
findings.tc_impact: The fiduciary signs a request listing '#32 Gilt overmantel mirror'. The ledger and the Court Inventory later list #32 as a different object. The approval itself is keyed by id and stays right, but the paper trail by number no longer lines up, and a careful trust officer will find it.
findings.proposal: Stop issuing a final number from a local high-water mark. The server assigns numbers in saveMediaStore (under the lock it already holds) and returns them, and the app draws an unsynced line as '#— (numbering)' and refuses to print a paper with one. A cheaper option: issue per device from a block (laptop 1-499, iPad 500-999, device id in Settings). Either way, item numbers never move.
findings.vnote:
Both devices were real app pages, and each pressed '+ Another item in this photo' before reading the other's save.
- A split e01's photograph and named the new line. B split e10's and named its line 'Gilt overmantel mirror'.
- Both new lines were issued #32. B's row showed 32, and B would print '#32 Gilt overmantel mirror'.
- After both read the sheet, both devices showed A's line as #32 and B's as #33. B's number moved after it was on screen and printable.

Code: _invAssignItemNos issues numbers off the local high-water mark and gives a collision to the earliest ts (29230-29272). A split takes its source photograph's ts.

This contradicts CLAUDE.md's 'Item numbers are permanent' for any number a paper has already cited.

findings.title: KNOWN: a press straight from a row's box is lost, and not only on the Releases card: the work bar's buttons and every Needs-you chip too
findings.where: _invEdit repaints by outerHTML or innerHTML on every change: the flag strip (_invRefreshFlagStrip, havellin.html:29839), the work bar on a figure or count (about 29835), the records, the guardrail and the releases. A change event fires on mousedown's blur, so the control under the pointer is replaced before mouseup.
findings.evidence: KNOWN: Open work records the lost press on the Releases card only (browser step 110 tabs out first). New reach, SYN/e9.js and e9b.js (out/e9.txt, e9b.txt): typing a Total and pressing 'No value yet' left the filter at ""; typing a name and pressing 'Not yet decided' did the same; typing a Total and pressing Estate Inventory PDF ran nothing ('first press ran []', 'second press ran ["printEstateInventoryReport"]'). The control case (Tab first, then the chip) worked.
findings.tc_impact: The evening's commonest motion is to type a value and press the next thing: a chip to jump to the next gap, Value N lines, the PDF. It fails silently about once per row, and the TC learns to double-press, which is exactly how Remove lines or Send request get pressed twice.
findings.proposal: Defer the by-id repaints of controls outside the row to the next tick after a pointerup (queue them in _invEdit and flush on setTimeout(0) after 'pointerup' or 'keyup'). Or repaint the counts by text node (the strong tag inside each chip, the work bar's counts) rather than replacing the buttons. Then the button under the pointer is the same element on mouseup.
findings.vnote:
The root cause is the known one (Open work: a Releases-card button pressed straight from a box is replaced under the pointer). The new reach is real; my results:
- Total typed, then 'No value yet' pressed: the first press left the filter at '', the second set 'noval'.
- Total typed, then Estate Inventory PDF pressed: the first press ran it 0 times, the second ran it.
- Name typed, then the 'Not yet decided' chip pressed: the first press did nothing.
- Name typed, then Estate Inventory PDF pressed: this worked first time, because _invEdit does not repaint the work bar on objectName.
- Control: Total typed, Tab, then the chip: worked.

So it hits the flag-strip chips after any edit, and the work bar after a figure or count edit. It is narrower than 'about once per row'.

findings.title: When an agent run finishes while the cursor sits in a box, the desk keeps saying 'Valuing…', shows the valued rows' Total boxes blank and still offers 'Value N lines'
findings.where: _avFinish ends with _invRenderWhenIdle (havellin.html:39008-39031) without first repainting the state line (_avRepaint, 39050) or the figures (_invPaintFigures). _invRenderWhenIdle waits for a focusout that never comes while the TC tabs from box to box (39035).
findings.evidence: SYN/e18.js, out/e18.txt: Agent Two answered while the TC typed in one Total box for 20 s. 23 of 24 valued rows showed a blank Total on screen ('valued 24, blankOnScreen 23'), the state line read 'Valuing… 24 of 24 · 4 sent on to research', and the work bar offered 'Value 24 lines'. After a click outside, the state line read 'Agent Two: 24 valued' and the button was gone. The same appeared in SYN/e5.js, op 1, after a rename.
findings.tc_impact: Working down the rows with Tab, the TC never sees Agent Two's figures arrive. They may type over a figure they cannot see, press Value N lines again (a lost press, SYN-12), or wait on a 'Valuing…' that finished minutes ago.
findings.proposal: In _avFinish, _agFinish and _arFinish, repaint by id whatever holds no box the person is in: the state line, each valued row's Each and Total (_invPaintFigures) unless that row holds the focus, and the flag strip. The full render stays held for focusout. The TC sees '24 valued' and the figures fill in around the box they are typing in.
findings.vnote:
1. I pressed 'Value 2 lines' with agentValue held, clicked into e18's name box, released the answer, then tabbed on twice.
2. The state line read 'Valuing… 2 of 2 · 1 sent on to research'. e20's and e23's Total boxes were blank on screen while the data held 350 and 40. The work bar still offered 'Value 2 lines'.
3. After a click outside, the state line read 'Agent Two: 2 valued · review them below', both boxes showed $350 and $40, and the button was gone.

Code: _avFinish ends with _invRenderWhenIdle (39031) and calls neither _avRepaint nor _invPaintFigures. _invRenderWhenIdle re-holds on every focusout while the next focused element is a box (39035-39046).

findings.title: Firearms set in an item's record does not redraw the row: the 'Possible NFA item' tick and the 'Not cleared to carry' panel appear only after a full redraw
findings.where: The record's Category select (_invEdit with key 'category', havellin.html:29700-29880). The row is redrawn only when the figure stops being the agent's, a plan vendor fills in, or the appraisal lands (about 29798). Category repaints the summary, the guardrail, the flag strip and the work bar, but not the row's badges or its record.
findings.evidence: SYN/e5c.js, out/e5c.txt (Hale, a living Home Transition): with #12 Lawn mower's record open, Category was set to Firearms. Shown: '🔌12 Electronics & Appliances · Garage · unsure' with no firearm section. findings.proposal: In _invEdit, redraw the row (and its open record) by id after category, flagDisputed, flagBequest, needsAppr, flagMAIV and maivCat edits, as it already does when the agent's figure changes hands. Its focus moves are already handled because these are selects and ticks, not text.
findings.vnote:
Hale (living), l12 Lawn mower. With its record open I set the record's Category select to Firearms. The data said Firearms, but the row still read 'Electronics & Appliances · Garage · unsure', with no flagNFA control and no 'held' or 'Not cleared to carry'. After a full render the row read 'Firearms · Garage · ⚠ held', with the NFA control and the held warning.

Code: _invEdit redraws the row only when an agent figure changes hands, a plan vendor fills in, or the appraised state flips (29798-29801). A category edit repaints the summary, guardrail, work bar, flag strip, records and releases, but not the row.

Medium, not higher: the transport gates are enforced in the handlers whatever the screen shows.

findings.title: The playbook promises 'two people working the same job keep both sets of edits'; the desk guide says nothing about two devices or that the tab does not re-read
findings.where: concierge-guide.html:1040 ('It now saves to the shared sheet and merges item by item, so two people working the same job keep both sets of edits'); evening-desk-guide.html (no device or reload guidance beyond the bars' 'loading…' and 'sheet unreachable').
findings.evidence: SYN-01's measurements (out/e2.txt, e6.txt) contradict the sentence for any line both touch, and for any agent run. The manual does say the newer whole record wins within an item, so the two documents disagree with each other.
findings.tc_impact: Anthony and Ashley are told it is safe to split a house across two devices, and the desk loses work exactly that way.
findings.proposal: Until SYN-01 lands, the playbook and The Evening Desk should say plainly: 'One person per client on the desk at a time. If the other device has been on it today, leave the tab and come back before you start, which reads the sheet. Two people on two clients is fine.' Once the per-field merge lands, rewrite both to say what then holds.
findings.vnote:
concierge-guide.html:1040 says: 'It now saves to the shared sheet and merges item by item, so two people working the same job keep both sets of edits.' That is true for different lines and false for the same line or any agent run (v1, v2). CONCIERGE_GUIDE.md:1023 matches.

The manual (manual.html:2385 and 2438) says the merge takes the whole newer record within an item, so the two documents disagree. evening-desk-guide.html covers only 'loading…' and 'sheet unreachable' and nothing about two devices on one client.

The proposed interim wording is a documentation change and conflicts with no Decided rule.

findings.title: Every manifest save reads and rewrites the whole MediaStore of every job ever worked, under the deployment-wide lock
findings.where: saveMediaStore: getMediaStore() reads the entire store (saveInventory.gs:656), merges one job and writes the whole blob back (_writeStoreBlob('MediaStore', store), saveInventory.gs:680), on every desk edit after the 2.5 s debounce and every agent batch.
findings.evidence: This is reasoning from the code, not measured here (no Apps Script). CLAUDE.md's own figures put a line at about 791 bytes once named and valued, so a 600-line house is about 0.5 MB and a 3,000-line estate about 2.5 MB. After a few estates, each desk keystroke burst rewrites several MB of chunked cells while holding the script lock every other write waits on.
findings.tc_impact: As the business grows, desk saves slow down. The lock times out ('busy'), the chip shows retrying, and SYN-06's stranding windows widen, all during the busiest evenings.
findings.proposal: Store each job's manifest in its own chunked range or tab (MediaStore:<jobId>), so a save reads and writes one job, as loadMedia already reads one. Measure a save on a 3,000-line seed with the editor's timer before and after, and print it in testAgentRoomCheck-style probe output.
findings.vnote:
Confirmed by code:
- saveMediaStore calls getMediaStore(), which is _readStoreBlob('MediaStore', {}) and reads the whole store (saveInventory.gs:425, 656).
- It then writes the whole blob back through _writeStoreBlob, which clears every row and rewrites every chunk (main-sync.gs:628-645), under the script lock taken by _lockOrBusy.

The consequences (slower saves, busy lock timeouts) are reasoning, not measured; there is no Apps Script here. The 791 bytes per line comes from MANUAL.md and BUILD_HISTORY.md, not CLAUDE.md. Rated low: at 1 to 5 jobs a month this grows slowly. The finding is still worth measuring before the store carries a year of estates.

findings.title: The offline chip says '1 unsaved change' for any number of desk edits
findings.where: updatePendingIndicator counts queued writes (havellin.html:42054, 42058). The whole manifest is one write key (main/saveMedia:<jobId>).

findings.proposal: For a manifest write, count the lines whose updatedAt is newer than the last successful save ('42 lines not yet on the sheet — retrying…'), recorded when the save lands.
findings.vnote:
With saveMedia aborting I made four edits: two names and two figures. The chip read '⚠ 1 unsaved change — retrying… ▸'.

Code: _pendingChipCopy counts the keys of _pendingWrites (42001 on). _writeKey collapses every manifest write for a job onto one key, 'main/saveMedia:<jobId>' (41966-41979).
